user.title: Pricing source
user.description: LibrePower core handles pricing and the optimiser. You'll also need a separate battery integration (e.g. librepower-powerwall) for it to actually see or control a battery - install that from HACS if you haven't already.

entity_bridge.title: Read prices from an existing integration
entity_bridge.description: Pick the sensors that hold your import and export price forecasts. This works out of the box with Amber Electric's official integration - no API key needed here, since Amber's own integration already handles that. If you're using a different integration and it doesn't work, the field names it expects can be adjusted afterwards in the integration options.

fixed_tariff.title: Fixed tariff
fixed_tariff.description: For a flat rate or time-of-use plan with no price API - enter the rates from your bill in dollars per kWh, GST inclusive. You can add peak and off-peak windows afterwards in the integration options.

error.entity_not_found: That entity doesn't exist. Check the source integration is set up and the entity ID is correct.

init.title: Control
init.description: While this is off, LibrePower runs in shadow mode: it plans a full schedule and publishes it to sensors, but never writes to the battery. That makes it safe to run alongside PowerSync or any other optimiser.

data.control_enabled: Allow LibrePower to control the battery

confirm_control.title: Hand control to LibrePower?
confirm_control.description:
Only one integration may control a battery. If another optimiser is still managing it, disable that first and confirm it has stopped writing.

Whether a write actually reaches the battery also depends on the registered battery adapter - some hardware/pairing modes support read-only telemetry but not control writes. Check that adapter's own documentation if control stays unavailable after enabling this.

Two optimisers on one battery will fight: each reads the other's change as an error and corrects it, and the battery cycles needlessly.

Leave the box unticked to stay in shadow mode.

data.understood: No other integration is controlling this Powerwall

tuning.title: Optimiser tuning
tuning.description:
Wear cost charges the optimiser for battery throughput so it won't chase arbitrage that costs more in cell degradation than it earns. Around 0.02 $/kWh is a reasonable starting point for LFP; set 0 to disable.

Weather-aware solar forecasting uses Open-Meteo (no account or API key needed) to adjust the history-based solar forecast for tomorrow's actual weather, rather than just typical conditions for the season. Off by default - the history-based forecast works fully offline either way; this only sharpens it. If Open-Meteo is unreachable, the integration silently falls back to history-only.

Battery capacity and charge/discharge limits are not set here - they're reported automatically by whichever battery adapter is registered.

bridge_fields.title: Price sensor field names
bridge_fields.description:
Only shown because your price source is 'read from an existing integration'. These default to Amber Electric's official integration's shape and normally don't need changing - override them only if you picked sensors from a different forecast-publishing integration (e.g. Octopus, an AEMO spot-price integration) whose attribute is named differently.

Forecast attribute: the sensor attribute holding the list of upcoming price intervals.
Start time field: the key in each interval for its start time.
Price field: the key in each interval for its price ($/kWh).

no_import_windows.title: No-import windows

data.action: What would you like to do?

add_no_import_window.title: Add a no-import window
add_no_import_window.description: Start is inclusive, end is exclusive. If end is earlier than start, the window is treated as wrapping past midnight (e.g. 22:00 -> 07:00). Leave the days blank to apply every day.

tou_windows.title: Time-of-use rate windows

data.action: What would you like to do?

add_tou_window.title: Add a rate window
add_tou_window.description: Start is inclusive, end is exclusive. If end is earlier than start, the window is treated as wrapping past midnight (e.g. 22:00 -> 07:00). Leave the days blank to apply every day. Rates are $/kWh, GST-inclusive, matching your bill - export rate can be negative if your plan charges you to export during this window.

error.window_zero_length: Start and end time can't be the same - that's neither "always" nor "never" as a window. Pick two different times.
